title: GST 111 (COOU) | Chapter Five: The Art of Effective Public Speaking: Types and Formats of Delivery
subject: GST 111

questions.question: Speech becomes a speech when it is?
questions.explanation: The chapter states that speech becomes a speech when it is presented.

questions.question: Planning is considered as one of the major keys to effective?
questions.explanation: Planning is considered one of the major keys to effective public speech.

questions.question: A well planned speech enables the speaker to deliver with?
questions.explanation: A well planned speech enables the speaker to deliver his speech with confidence.

questions.question: Finegan (2012) sees speech as a primary mode of?
questions.explanation: Finegan (2012) sees speech as a primary mode of human language.

questions.question: According to Okoroafor (2004), it is the audience that determines the purpose of the?
questions.explanation: Okoroafor (2004) collaborates with Litfin (1992) that it is the audience that determines the purpose of the speech.

questions.question: Which of these is a type of speech according to its purpose?
questions.explanation: The three types of purposes of speech correspond to informative, persuasive and entertaining speeches.

questions.question: The basic components of every speech include the speaker, an audience and the desire of the former to influence the latter's thoughts, beliefs and?
questions.explanation: Alimole (2002) asserts that the basic components include the speaker, an audience and the desire of the former to influence the latter's thoughts, beliefs and behaviour.

questions.question: Public speakers succeed by employing rhetorical features to create the desired impression and to?
questions.explanation: Public speakers employ rhetorical features to create the desired impression and to persuade their audience to change their initial positions and beliefs.

questions.question: According to Carlin and Payne (1995), public speaking is ranked as which level of communication?
questions.explanation: Public speaking is ranked by Carlin and Payne (1995) as the fourth level of communication.

questions.question: The fourth level of communication is defined as a situation where one person is communicating with?
questions.explanation: The fourth level is defined as a situation where one person is communicating with many.

questions.question: In the fourth level of communication, most of the audience's feedback is?
questions.explanation: In the fourth level of communication, most of the audience's feedback is nonverbal.

questions.question: What makes a successful speech is?
questions.explanation: What makes a successful speech is good planning.

questions.question: Public speeches that are meant to inform should be planned in line with the maxim of?
questions.explanation: Informative speeches should be planned and presented in line with the maxim of quantity.

questions.question: The maxim of quantity was given by?
questions.explanation: The maxim of quantity is a maxim given by H.P. Grice.

questions.question: The sole purpose of informative speech is to clarify, explain and?
questions.explanation: The sole purpose of informative speech is to clarify, explain, describe the audience's knowledge about some concept.

questions.question: In informative speech, the goal is to enable the audience to grasp and then ______ the material.
questions.explanation: The goal of informative speech is to enable the audience to grasp and then retain the material.

questions.question: Persuasive speech requires a greater mastery of the process of?
questions.explanation: Persuasive speech requires a greater mastery and awareness of the process of reasoning.

questions.question: The speech writer exhibits the art of effective use of the resources of language called?
questions.explanation: The speech writer exhibits the art of effective use of the resources of language (rhetoric).

questions.question: Which of these is an artistic method of appeal?
questions.explanation: Aristotle refers to pathos, ethos and logos as artistic methods of appeals.

questions.question: Logos appeals to the audience's?
questions.explanation: Logos appeals to the audience's rationality through facts or reasons.

questions.question: Pathos appeals to the audience's?
questions.explanation: Pathos appeals to the audience's emotion.

questions.question: Ethos proves the speaker's or writer's?
questions.explanation: Ethos proves the speaker's or writer's credibility and fidelity to the audience.

questions.question: The goal of persuasive speech is to change some belief or attitude of the audience in some ______ way.
questions.explanation: The goal of persuasive speech is to change some belief or attitude of the audience in some predetermined way.

questions.question: In the speech to actuate, the goal is to?
questions.explanation: In the speech to actuate, the goal is to mobilize the audience and impel them to action.

questions.question: Eko (2002) identifies how many strategies for persuasive argument?
questions.explanation: Eko (2002) identifies three strategies for persuasive argument.

questions.question: Entertaining speeches help people to relax in occasions like graduation parties, birthday parties and?
questions.explanation: Entertaining speeches are used in occasions like graduation parties, birthday parties, end of year (get-together) parties.

questions.question: A speechwriter aiming to entertain may explore jokes, anecdotes, curious bits of information and?
questions.explanation: A speechwriter aiming to entertain may explore jokes, anecdotes, curious bits of information, and even satire.

questions.question: Good speakers introduce jokes during all speech situations particularly when listeners show signs of?
questions.explanation: Good speakers introduce jokes particularly when listeners show signs of weariness or boredom to revive and sustain their interest.

questions.question: A moment of getting set both for you and for your audience is very?
questions.explanation: A moment of getting set both for you and for your audience is very important.

questions.question: Your appearance tells on your background, personality and builds?
questions.explanation: Your appearance tells on your background, personality and builds good will or destroys you.

questions.question: Being brief in speech should not be at the detriment of?
questions.explanation: Be as brief as possible in your speech but not at the detriment of clarity.

questions.question: Your speech should be long enough to achieve its objectives, part of which is?
questions.explanation: Your speech should be long enough to achieve its objectives, part of which is clarity of meaning.

questions.question: Adjust your speed of delivery in accordance with the audience's capability to?
questions.explanation: Adjust your speed of delivery in accordance with the audience's capability to listen.

questions.question: Your voice should be animated and vigorous, sonorous and?
questions.explanation: Your voice should be animated and vigorous, sonorous and energetic.

questions.question: Articulate your sounds distinctly and accurately by pronouncing all your vowels and?
questions.explanation: Articulate your sounds distinctly and accurately by pronouncing all your vowels and consonants.

questions.question: To overcome stage fright, you should relax your muscles and your?
questions.explanation: To overcome stage fright, relax your muscles and your mind too.

questions.question: Think of your audience as being composed of?
questions.explanation: Think of your audience as being composed of friendly individuals and not tigers or wolves.

questions.question: Control your anger or temper especially when dealing with a?
questions.explanation: Control your anger especially when dealing with a hostile audience or an audience that is not entirely friendly.

questions.question: Body language is an essential part of?
questions.explanation: Body language is an essential part of speech.

questions.question: Use gestures, facial expressions and other forms of body movements to put your ______ across.
questions.explanation: Use gestures, facial expressions and other forms of body movements to put your meanings across.

questions.question: Observe pauses preferably between sentences, phrases and?
questions.explanation: Observe pauses where applicable, preferably between sentences, phrases and clauses.

questions.question: Speech depends extensively on?
questions.explanation: Speech depends extensively on breath.

questions.question: Summarise your main points at the ______ of your speech.
questions.explanation: Summarise your main points at the end of your speech.

questions.question: Delivery refers to the method of presenting the speech rather than the verbal and nonverbal?
questions.explanation: Delivery refers to the method of presenting the speech rather than the verbal and nonverbal presentation.

questions.question: Which of these is a format of speech delivery?
questions.explanation: The formats of delivery are manuscript, impromptu, extemporaneous and memorised.

questions.question: Speeches that are written down and read out to the audience are delivered in?
questions.explanation: Speeches written down and read out to the audience are delivered in manuscript.

questions.question: Manuscript delivery requires a speaker to write out every word of a?
questions.explanation: Manuscript delivery requires a speaker to write out every word of a speech.

questions.question: Public figures like political speakers use manuscripts for several reasons including the need to make consistent?
questions.explanation: Public figures use manuscripts because they need to make consistent statements.

questions.question: One advantage of manuscript delivery is that the presenter will not forget any of the?
questions.explanation: Since manuscript speeches are written down and read to the audience, the presenter will not forget any of the points.

questions.question: Impromptu delivery requires the least?
questions.explanation: Impromptu delivery requires the least preparation because they are made on the spur of the moment.
